definition: Also known as Glorot initialization, this technique provides an effective way to initialize the weights of a neural network to help prevent the vanishing or exploding gradient problems during training.
details: Also known as Glorot initialization, this technique provides an effective way to initialize the weights of a neural network to help prevent the vanishing or exploding gradient problems during training.

explainer.lead: Xavier's initialization, also called Glorot initialization, sets neural network starting weights to prevent vanishing or exploding gradients. It matters because it helps deep networks train reliably from the first step.

tiers.eli5: It is like tuning every instrument to the same level before the orchestra plays, so no section drowns out the rest.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a default weight initializer for deep networks to keep gradients in a workable range. The pitfall is assuming it suits every architecture; activation choice and depth can make another scheme preferable.
tiers.paperLevel: Weights are initialized so that activation and gradient variance are preserved across layers, with scaling based on input and output unit counts. It targets vanishing and exploding gradients but does not remove them in all architectures.

explainer.example: A fully connected layer with many inputs and fewer outputs gets weights scaled to its fan-in and fan-out, so forward signals neither vanish nor explode.
